b-stable-position-reconstruction.rationale: New A6 Behavior for a mechanism that was initially suspected of being defective and turned out to be handled: the node's effective last index/entry is the maximum of the log and snapshot positions. Independently addable; no existing object's meaning changes.

f-stable-log-position.rationale: New A6 Fact giving the log/snapshot position its own identity and validity context, so that future questions about recovery, compaction or index reuse do not have to re-derive it. No existing Fact's meaning changes.

feedback.answered: A suspected defect was investigated and explained rather than escalated. A node whose log is empty but which holds a newer snapshot - the state RecoverCluster deliberately produces by truncating the whole log, and also reachable with TrailingLogs=0 when the FSM has applied through the snapshot index - looked as if it would restart at log index 0, reuse indices below the snapshot and leave committed client entries unapplied and unanswered. It does not: getLastIndex returns max(lastLogIndex, lastSnapshotIndex) and getLastEntry returns the snapshot's index/term when the snapshot is newer (state.go:157-174), while NewRaft reads the log's last index and restoreSnapshot sets lastApplied and the last snapshot (api.go:631-664). The node therefore advertises and resumes at the snapshot index, and dispatchLogs starts from getLastIndex()+1. The map gains the mechanism as behavior b-stable-position-reconstruction and fact f-stable-log-position so the false lead is closed with sources instead of being re-investigated.
remaining: ReloadConfig notification scope remains a low-consequence lead: only a decreased HeartbeatTimeout signals the notify channels, so a decreased LeaderLeaseTimeout is not picked up until the current lease timer fires (api.go:713-741, config.go:260-290).

The three confirmed findings each keep an open premise: real-deployment reachability for the unconfigured TimeoutNow sender, the election consequence of the heartbeat fast path, and whether batching FSMs are contractually exempt from ConfigurationStore.

Unread or partly read areas with no question yet: observer plumbing, the file and in-memory snapshot stores, net_transport beyond the heartbeat classification, and the concurrency contract of processHeartbeat.
feedback.rationale: Recording an explained mechanism in the support layer closes a lead without inflating it into a Candidate, and it gives later recovery/compaction questions a sourced identity for the log/snapshot position instead of leaving them to re-derive the max-of-two rule. The core overview is unchanged, since this is a support mechanism rather than a formation or authority relationship.

rationale: Research product recording an explained support mechanism (effective last index/entry is max of log and snapshot) as a new behavior and fact, closing a false lead about index reuse after recovery or full compaction. The draft map (base version 9) adds only those two objects and one source; no meaning, identity, edge, requirement or previously accepted Surface disposition changes, so the three confirmed findings and every accepted result keep their original basis. The ReloadConfig lead and the open reachability premises of the confirmed findings are preserved unchanged in the remaining list.
